Nothing exceptional: disappointed by the expectations, disorganization, and dishes that need to be reconsidered.
Aug 2026 • Couples
I must preface this by saying that I am a person who almost always tends to leave very positive reviews and value effort, but unfortunately, this was the first real disappointment after 15 fantastic days in Vietnam. It is the first place of our trip where we didn't have a "wow" meal and where I would never return.
The positive points and the local cuisine:
The place is cute and clean. A positive note for the goat, the famous specialty typical of the Ninh Binh area: it was good and flavorful, a dish that in my opinion is worth trying if you are open to flavors different from those we are used to in the West. The coconut ice cream to finish was also very good.
The sore points and the disorganization:
For the rest, the high expectations created by the many positive reviews were not confirmed at all. The chicken with cashews was a complete disaster: served totally soupy and, incredibly, arrived without cashews! We were practically brought chicken with peppers drowned in broth and we had to explicitly ask at the table for them to bring us the forgotten cashews. The Morning Glory (the sautéed vegetables) also arrived immersed in broth, which is definitely uncommon and unpleasant to the palate.
The service is poorly organized and the staff, although they try, have a level of English that is decidedly lower and less fluent than the average found in many other places in the country, making even basic communication about missing dishes difficult.
In summary: it is not to be completely dismissed because some dishes are saved, but overall it is a mediocre, disorganized experience and absolutely not up to the standard of the renowned Vietnamese cuisine tried elsewhere.

Thank you for taking the time to share such detailed feedback. We are sorry that your experience did not meet your expectations, especially after seeing so many positive reviews.

We sincerely apologize for the cashew chicken being served without the cashews and for both the chicken and morning glory being too watery. That is not how these dishes should be prepared, and we have already discussed this with our kitchen team to make sure we pay closer attention to the consistency and final check of each dish before it is served.

We are also sorry that communication with our team was difficult. We understand how frustrating this can be when something is missing from a dish, and we will continue working on both staff training and English communication.

At the same time, we are glad to hear that you enjoyed the local goat dish, the coconut ice cream, and found the restaurant clean and pleasant.

Thank you again for your honest feedback. Even when a review is difficult to read, it helps us see where we need to improve.

Vietnamese Gem
May 2026 • Friends
Stayed several days in Tam Coc (Ninh Binh), and we were fortunate to find this family-run restaurant on our first evening. It would appear to be run by father (in the kitchen cooking), mother (supervising the restaurant), and their family waiting at the tables. The establishment occupies two floors with adequate restroom facilities on both floors.

The staff are friendly, welcoming and efficient, and both understand and speak English well.

There is an extensive menu of traditional Vietnamese dishes, all of which are prepared fresh to order. The fresh spring rolls are particularly good as a starter.

This establishment is highly recommended to anyone staying in the Ninh Binh area.
